plan: My private value is $10, which means I want to win only if the item can be purchased for less than my value. My optimal strategy is to bid slightly above my true value to increase my chances of winning, but not so high that I risk negative earnings. Since values are randomly drawn and this is a one-round game, I'll bid $10.50 - this gives me a small buffer above my value while signaling I'm willing to compete.

My private value is $30. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is typically to bid my true value. This means bidding $30 ensures I only win if the item is worth at least that much to me. If I win at a lower price, I make a profit. If I lose, it means another bidder valued the item more highly. With no prior round history, a true-value bid is the most rational approach.

My private value is $25, which means I want to maximize my potential profit. Since this is a single round with no prior history, I'll use a strategic bid slightly below my true value. Bidding exactly at $25 risks paying close to my entire value. I'll bid $22, which gives me some potential profit margin if I win. This allows me to potentially win at a price below my value while not overbidding and risking paying more than the item is worth to me.
